title: Detect and heal ghost fragment charges from delayed/out-of-order streaming frames
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We intermittently observe so-called 'ghost' charges where customers are billed for output tokens that are later replayed or re-ordered from delayed stream fragments. These manifest after network reconnects, client retries with overlapping fragments, and when archive/backfill workers re-ingest fragments without proper dedupe heuristics. The outcome is occasional double-charging, customer complaints, and expensive manual audit to refund credits.

Goal: Implement deterministic detection of ghost fragment charges and an automated heal path that: 1) flags suspected duplicate fragment charges, 2) computes corrective adjustments (refunds/prorates), and 3) maintains an auditable trail so support can review and approve automated refunds. Keep detection conservative by default and dark-launch telemetry before automatic refunds.

Scope: Changes span streaming-ingestor (sequence/fragment tracking), accounting-processor (single charge canonicalization), a backfill/repair worker for historical corrections, and Console dashboards + alerts. This ticket covers scoping, instrumentation, the detection algorithm, unit/integration tests, and a staged rollout plan.
investigation:
Repro: crafted a client that simulates: 1) send prefix A (tokens 0-50), network drop, 2) reconnect and resend prefix A (duplicate frames with same payload), 3) later a delayed fragment arrives for tokens 0-10 with a different chunking boundary. Observed charges: both initial and resumed sessions produced non-idempotent accounting entries.

Logs: session_id, frame_seq, frame_checksum, and ingest_timestamp show duplicates with non-monotonic ingest_timestamp and overlapping token ranges. Accounting entries use (session_id, charge_window_id) and currently do not include fragment_checksum dedupe.

Hypothesis: Duplicate charges occur when accounting-processor receives fragments with overlapping token ranges and different fragment ids; without a canonicalization step keyed by checksum+seq-range we cannot reliably dedupe across retries and reconnects.
decisions:
1) Use a canonical fragment key composed of (session_id, seq_range_start, seq_range_end, checksum) and record the canonicalizer outcome atomically in the charges table before emitting billing records.
2) Introduce a small fragment watermark cache (LRU with TTL) in streaming-ingestor to aggressively dedupe recent fragments for low latency flows.
3) For older fragments (>48h) rely on a backfill repair worker to detect probable duplicates via overlap heuristics and apply corrections as audit actions rather than immediate refunds.
4) Dark-launch the detector as a monitoring-only signal for 7 days before enabling automatic refunds.
5) Provide a support UI view to approve or rollback corrections.
implementation_notes:
Code touchpoints: streaming-ingestor (ingest/fragments), accounting-processor (emit_charge_record), metering-db schema (charges table + fragment_index), backfill-worker (repair/heuristics), console (audit view + metric panels).

DB changes: add fragment_index table with columns: fragment_key (pk), session_id, seq_start, seq_end, checksum, canonical_charge_id, first_seen_ts. Add charges.canonicalized boolean and correction_applied_at timestamp. Migration plan: run backfill to populate fragment_index for last 30 days before enabling canonicalization writes.

Heuristic for backfill detection: if two fragments for same session overlap by >10% token range or exact checksum match and charges were both emitted, mark the older as candidate_ghost. Compute refund_amount = charged_amount * overlap_fraction and create a correction record referencing both charges.

Performance: canonicalization check must be sub-ms for hot paths. Use in-memory shard cache keyed by session hashed to single writer to avoid cross-writer races. Fallback to DB with optimistic insert using unique constraint on fragment_key.
test_plan:
Unit tests: fragment_key generation, checksum collision resistance (randomized inputs), canonicalization race conditions (concurrent inserts).
Integration tests: synthetic client that exercises reconnects, duplicate sends, delayed fragments, and archive replays. Verify final net charge equals single canonicalized charge.
E2E: simulate 1000 sessions with 1-3 reconnects and measure ghost_charges_detected=0 after repair.
QA: create a support sandbox with stored sessions to validate UI and manual correction flow.
Telemetry assertions: counters for ghost_charges_detected (must decline after fix), correction_actions_created, correction_auto_applied, correction_manual_approved, correction_latency_ms (histogram).
acceptance_criteria: No new double-charge incidents for simulated reconnect/replay scenarios in E2E runs
Detector exposed as monitoring-only for 7 days with stable false-positive rate <0.5% of total charges
Backfill worker produces auditable correction records for historical duplicates and test coverage exists for repair logic
Dashboard panel showing ghost_charges_detected incrementing and link to support UI per-customer
Migration completed for last 30 days with no blocking anomalies and DB write path is backward compatible
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (dark launch): deploy canonicalization writes to a parallel 'detector' path that does not alter billing, emit telemetry only, 7 days.
Phase 1 (manual correction): enable backfill worker to create correction records as 'pending' actions in support UI; do not auto-apply. Monitor for false positives 3 days.
Phase 2 (auto-heal opt-in): allow small customers (<$200/mo) to opt-in for automated repairs for low friction. Monitor metrics for 7 days.
Phase 3 (global auto-heal): enable system-wide automatic corrections with throttling (max corrections/hour) and audit logs. Rollback knob in Console if anomalies.
Kill-switch: runtime flag 'metering.ghost_heal.enabled' default false until Phase 2.
metrics_and_alerting:
New metrics: ghost_charges_detected.count, ghost_corrections_created.count, correction_auto_apply_success.count, correction_auto_apply_fail.count, fragment_canonicalization_latency.ms (p50/p95/p99).
Alerts: P1 if ghost_charges_detected > 5/min over 30m window or correction_auto_apply_fail.rate > 1% over 1h.
Dashboards: per-model and per-region breakdown and per-customer top offenders. Include sample logs for forensic debugging: session_id, fragment_key, seq_range, checksum, ingest_ts, charge_id.
